sheet-1-1.description: The middle of three strips into which Sheet 1 cuts the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike through the village of Haskell, in what is now the Borough of Wanaque. The strip runs north and south between match line A-B at its top, which continues on the left strip of the sheet, and match line C-D at its foot, which continues on the right strip. The turnpike is drawn 34 to 40 ft wide with alternate house numbers 23 to 45 on the west side and 75 to 92 on the east side. The only cross street is an unnamed 40 ft street leading east from the turnpike about the middle of the strip, which the georeferencing takes to be today's Smith Avenue. North of it on the east side stands G. Venezia's Park Hotel, a two-and-a-half-storey frame building with a saloon and several outbuildings; Venezia Lane now runs near its site. The rest of the strip is a loose row of frame dwellings, most of two storeys, with sheds, an auto house, a vacant shop, an ice house, a poultry house and a foundation without a building, set in deep lots whose side lines are drawn to the heavy strip borders marked No Exposure. A key to the map symbols is printed in the lower left of the strip and is left out of the mask. The strip is drawn at 50 ft to an inch; the north arrows on the sheet point nearly straight up, while the road itself runs about 12 degrees east of north here.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.

The unnamed 40 ft cross street east of the turnpike is taken to be Smith Avenue; the hotel then falls about 40 m from today's Venezia Lane, and the Haskell Public School on the next strip falls on the site of Haskell Elementary School.
G. Venezia's Park Hotel stood on the east side of the turnpike north of the cross street.

sheet-1-2.description: The northern strip of Sheet 1, on the left of the page: the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, marked Macadam Paved, from match line A-B at its foot (which continues on the middle strip) north to the edge of the sheet, where a note gives half a mile to Wanaque. It lies at the northern end of Haskell, in today's Borough of Wanaque. The turnpike is drawn about 33 to 34 ft wide, with alternate house numbers 46 to 62 on the west side and 93 to 111 on the east side. The Wanaque River crosses the top of the strip east of the road, drawn in blue between banks and lettered. Buildings are scattered: Mooney's Road House, a two-and-a-half-storey frame saloon with an ice house near it, a wagon shed, a concrete-block dwelling (shown in blue), a vacant shop, an ice house and frame dwellings of one to two storeys, several with stables or sheds. The lots on both sides reach to blank areas marked No Exposure. A small location map of New Jersey with the town underlined sits in the lower left corner and is left out of the mask, as is the part of the key printed over the strip border. The strip is drawn at 50 ft to an inch; on the ground the road runs about 17 degrees east of north here, while it is drawn nearly straight up the page, so the strip is turned against the others of the sheet.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.
A note at the top of the strip reads 1/2 Mile to Wanaque.
Placed from a single point carried from part 1 at match line A-B, with rotation from the modern line of Ringwood Avenue.

sheet-1-3.description: The southern strip of Sheet 1, on the right of the page: the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike from match line C-D at its top (which continues on the middle strip) south to a heavy line where a note gives a quarter of a mile to Sheet 2. It covers the centre of Haskell, in today's Borough of Wanaque, with alternate house numbers 16 to 25 on the west side and 64 to 73 on the east side of a road drawn 40 ft wide. At the top of the strip on the west side stands the Haskell Public School, a frame building heated by steam, on what is now the site of Haskell Elementary School. The rest of the strip is a row of frame dwellings, most of one and a half to two and a half storeys, in deep lots that run back to blank land marked No Exposure. The Sanborn title cartouche, giving a population of 700, prevailing winds, private wells and one chemical engine, sits in the upper right corner, and notes on water facilities and the volunteer fire company, with its chemical engine on wheels and help from Pompton Lakes, are printed west of the road. The strip is drawn at 50 ft to an inch; the road runs about 11 degrees east of north here but is drawn straight up the page.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.
Haskell Public School stood on the west side of the turnpike, where Haskell Elementary School is today.
A note at the foot of the strip reads 1/4 Mile to Sheet No. 2; the placement leaves a gap of about 180 m to Sheet 2, less than a quarter mile.
Placed from a single point carried from part 1 at match line C-D, with rotation from the modern line of Ringwood Avenue.

sheet-2-1.description: The left strip of Sheet 2 south of Doty Road: the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, drawn 40 ft wide, from its junction with Doty Road south to match mark 2 at the foot of the page, where it continues on the right strip of the sheet. This is the southern part of Haskell, in today's Borough of Wanaque, with alternate house numbers 125 to 135 on the west side and 164 to 176 on the east side. Doty Road, 30 ft wide, leaves the turnpike westward at the top of the part with a rounded corner, and a note at its western end gives about 500 ft to the Haskell Quarry Co., shown in a detail on Sheet 1. Development is thin: on the west side a few dwellings, two of them of concrete block (shown in blue), and a vacant store; on the east side a frame dwelling and a two-storey outbuilding in otherwise empty land running back to a heavy strip border marked No Exposure. A compass rose and the scale of feet are printed in the lower middle of the sheet. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch. On the ground the road runs about 5 degrees west of north here, while it is drawn straight up the page.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.
The sheet is split at Doty Road into two parts because the drawn bend of the turnpike there is about 9 degrees flatter than the modern road.
Placed from the Doty Road junction alone, with rotation from the lines measured there.

Scale 50 ft. Two strips of the turnpike: left strip with the Doty Road junction (split there into part 1, south, and part 2, north, because the drawn bend of the turnpike at Doty Road is about 9 deg flatter than the modern road), Road to Powder Mill and the Erie R.R. switch to the powder mill at the top; right strip (part 3), the continuation south, joined at match mark 2. Placed from the one junction and a carried match-mark point.

sheet-2-2.description: The left strip of Sheet 2 north of Doty Road: the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, here bending north-east, from the Doty Road junction to the Road to Powder Mill and the top of the page, where a note gives about a quarter of a mile to Sheet 1. This is the business corner of Haskell, in today's Borough of Wanaque, with alternate house numbers 136 to 143 on the west side and 177 to 183 on the east side. On the north-west corner of the junction stand the Haskell House, a two-storey saloon and hall of stone and concrete, and beside it the Fire Dept. of Progressive Eng. Co. No. 1, with one 40 gallon chemical engine on wheels, and a vacant store. Further north on the west side are a pool and barber shop, a general store and post office, frame dwellings and another pool and barber shop. Doty Road, 30 ft wide, runs west along the foot of the part with a stone dwelling and its stables near its western end. At the top the Road to Powder Mill crosses the turnpike eastward, with a switch from the Erie R.R. to the powder mill drawn beside it. The east side of the road is almost empty. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.
The Road to Powder Mill has no modern counterpart in the reference data; it lies between today's 3rd and 4th Avenues.
A switch track from the Erie R.R. to the powder mill runs alongside the Road to Powder Mill.
Placed from the Doty Road junction carried from part 1, with rotation from the modern line of Ringwood Avenue north of Doty Road.

sheet-2-3.description: The right strip of Sheet 2: the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike continued south from match mark 2 at the top of the page, where it joins the foot of the left strip, to the bottom of the sheet. It covers the southern end of Haskell toward Pompton Lakes, in today's Borough of Wanaque. The road is drawn 40 ft wide with alternate house numbers 101 to 124 on the west side and 144 to 163 on the east side. The northern half is the denser part of the strip: on the west side a saloon, a meat market and general store, further general stores, a cobbler and frame dwellings with sheds; on the east side dwellings, a fruit store, a general store with an oven and a small outbuilding behind, and stables. South of these the east side is a regular row of two-storey frame dwellings, one of concrete block, in long lots, and the west side has only a few dwellings and an auto house. A wind mill and tank stands back from the road on the east side, and a large frame dwelling, a wagon house and stables stand near the foot of the sheet. Lot lines on the east side run back to unbuilt land. The strip is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, and the road runs about 5 degrees west of north here.
notes: The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is Ringwood Avenue (County Route 511) today.
Placed from a single point carried from part 1 at match mark 2, where the left strip ends, with rotation from the modern line of Ringwood Avenue; the drawn lot lines east of the road are not streets.
